views.name: dogs_active_projection
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  dog_id,
  owner_id,
  abandoned_yn,
  breed_code,
  size_code,
  name,
  age,
  gender,
  weight,
  date_of_birth,
  date_arrived,
  date_adopted,
  date_departed
FROM Dogs
WHERE 1=1
views.description: Canonical projection of the Dogs table with stable, passthrough columns kept verbatim and common cleaning: preserves nullable foreign keys and converts boolean-like flags to canonical 'Y'/'N' where possible. Use this as the dog-level base for joins, cohorts, and aggregations. | Use for: List dogs with their attributes for joining/enrichment; Filter cohorts by arrival/adoption/departure dates; Compute dog-level aggregates (count, avg weight) after joins

views.name: owners_contact_projection
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  owner_id,
  first_name,
  last_name,
  street,
  city,
  state,
  zip_code,
  email_address,
  home_phone,
  cell_number
FROM Owners
WHERE 1=1
views.description: Projection of Owners retaining contact and identity columns verbatim. Use when enriching dog or treatment records with owner contact information. | Use for: Enrich dog records with owner contact details; Build owner-level reports (counts of dogs by owner, contact lists)

views.name: treatments_events
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  treatment_id,
  dog_id,
  professional_id,
  treatment_type_code,
  date_of_treatment,
  cost_of_treatment
FROM Treatments
WHERE 1=1
views.description: Event-level projection of Treatments with event timestamp and cost passthrough. Use as the canonical treatment fact for joins and time-based analysis. | Use for: Cost/time series of treatments; Join treatments to dogs/professionals for enriched event detail; Aggregate treatments by type, professional, or dog

views.name: dogs_with_lookups
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  D.dog_id,
  D.owner_id,
  D.abandoned_yn,
  D.breed_code,
  Breeds.breed_name,
  D.size_code,
  Sizes.size_description,
  D.name,
  D.age,
  D.gender,
  D.weight,
  D.date_of_birth,
  D.date_arrived,
  D.date_adopted,
  D.date_departed
FROM Dogs D
LEFT JOIN Breeds ON D.breed_code = Breeds.breed_code
LEFT JOIN Sizes ON D.size_code = Sizes.size_code
views.description: Denormalized dog-level relation enriched with Breed and Size descriptive labels and Owner id preserved. One row per dog. Good for dog lists and owner-facing reports that need breed/size text. | Use for: Display dogs with breed and size names; Create cohorts by breed_name or size_description; Join to treatments/professionals while keeping descriptive attributes

views.name: treatments_with_professional_and_type
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  T.treatment_id,
  T.dog_id,
  T.professional_id,
  Professionals.first_name,
  Professionals.last_name,
  T.treatment_type_code,
  Treatment_Types.treatment_type_description,
  T.date_of_treatment,
  T.cost_of_treatment
FROM Treatments T
LEFT JOIN Professionals ON T.professional_id = Professionals.professional_id
LEFT JOIN Treatment_Types ON T.treatment_type_code = Treatment_Types.treatment_type_code
views.description: Enriched treatment events joined to Professionals and Treatment_Types to expose professional identity and treatment descriptions alongside event measures. One row per treatment event. | Use for: Analyze treatment counts/costs by professional or treatment type; List treatment histories for a dog including professional names; Compute average cost per treatment type or per professional

views.name: dog_treatment_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  T.dog_id,
  COUNT(*) AS treatment_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(T.cost_of_treatment,0)) AS total_treatment_cost,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(COALESCE(T.cost_of_treatment,0))*1.0/COUNT(*) END AS avg_cost_per_treatment
FROM Treatments T
GROUP BY T.dog_id
views.description: Aggregated measures at the dog level: total number of treatments, total cost, and average cost per treatment. One row per dog. Use for per-dog cost analysis and ranking. | Use for: Which dogs incurred the highest treatment costs?; Average cost per treatment by dog; Filter dogs by having at least one treatment (join treatment_count > 0)

views.name: professional_treatment_aggregates
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  T.professional_id,
  COUNT(*) AS treatments_performed,
  SUM(COALESCE(T.cost_of_treatment,0)) AS total_cost_handled,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(COALESCE(T.cost_of_treatment,0))*1.0/COUNT(*) END AS avg_cost_per_treatment
FROM Treatments T
GROUP BY T.professional_id
views.description: Aggregated measures at the professional level: number of treatments performed, total and average cost of treatments they performed. One row per professional. Useful for workload and billing analytics. | Use for: Workload by professional; Which professionals handled the most/most expensive treatments?; Link professionals to HR/compensation analytics

views.name: latest_treatment_per_dog
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.treatment_id,
  t.dog_id,
  t.professional_id,
  t.treatment_type_code,
  t.date_of_treatment,
  t.cost_of_treatment
FROM (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY dog_id ORDER BY date_of_treatment DESC, treatment_id DESC) AS rn
  FROM Treatments
) t
WHERE t.rn = 1
views.description: Latest treatment event per dog (most recent date_of_treatment). One row per dog including the treatment_id and date. Use for last-visit reports and recency-based cohorts. | Use for: Find each dog's most recent treatment; Compute time since last treatment by joining to Dogs; Filter dogs by recency of treatment

views.name: treatment_time_series_by_day
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  date_of_treatment AS treatment_date,
  COUNT(*) AS treatments_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(cost_of_treatment,0)) AS total_cost
FROM Treatments
GROUP BY date_of_treatment
views.description: Daily aggregated treatment counts and total cost. One row per date_of_treatment (calendar day). Useful for time series and trend analysis. | Use for: Plot daily treatment volume or revenue; Detect seasonal patterns in treatments; Feed into moving averages or anomaly detection

views.name: dogs_with_treatment_summary
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  D.dog_id,
  D.owner_id,
  D.name,
  D.breed_code,
  B.breed_name,
  D.size_code,
  S.size_description,
  agg.treatment_count,
  agg.total_treatment_cost,
  agg.avg_cost_per_treatment
FROM Dogs D
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    T.dog_id,
    COUNT(*) AS treatment_count,
    SUM(COALESCE(T.cost_of_treatment,0)) AS total_treatment_cost,
    CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN NULL ELSE SUM(COALESCE(T.cost_of_treatment,0))*1.0/COUNT(*) END AS avg_cost_per_treatment
  FROM Treatments T
  GROUP BY T.dog_id
) agg ON D.dog_id = agg.dog_id
LEFT JOIN Breeds B ON D.breed_code = B.breed_code
LEFT JOIN Sizes S ON D.size_code = S.size_code
views.description: Dog-level relation joining dog attributes with their treatment aggregates (counts and costs). One row per dog including treatment metrics; missing treatments yield NULLs for aggregates. | Use for: Rank dogs by total treatment cost; List dogs with their treatment summaries and breed/size descriptions; Filter dogs by having no treatments (treatment_count IS NULL or 0)
